digest.component_or_area: tickets store initialization and CI workflow
propositions: Fresh full clone of tickets costs 1.04 GiB / 59s wall whereas --filter=blob:none costs 68.7 MiB / 14.3s (~15x reduction), but rebar cannot apply filters to clones it does not perform.

In Claude Code web environment, a timed-out tickets fetch causes rebar init to silently bootstrap a fresh empty orphan store that diverges from origin/tickets, causing all reads to return empty and writes to land on an un-fast-forwardable branch.

blob:none partial clone is safe for rebar's verify-identity access patterns because tree-level diff and event/keyring body reads come from the working tree, not lazy blobs, though git blame on historical trees will fault in blobs during the fail-close code path.

The CI reconcile-bridge workflow requires merge.ours.driver=true to be set before blob:none filter is applied, otherwise the merge.ours directive on .bridge_state/* silently degrades to a 3-way text merge of an 18 MB JSON file.
A simulated fetch failure must cause non-zero exit and prevent orphan branch creation to fix P1 bug where fail-open bootstrap diverges the store.
The introduced-commit map build during ENFORCED mode may fault in trees under blob:none and should be re-measured before authentication enforcement is re-enabled from advisory mode.
